# Elastic Security integration with Google Distributed Cloud: Closing the velocity gap in air-gapped environments


By


[TJ Banasik](https://www.elastic.co/blog/author/tj-banasik)[Mike Nichols](https://www.elastic.co/blog/author/mike-nichols)


October 16, 2026

The rules of cyber defense have shifted. Threat actors are increasingly using advanced automation to accelerate reconnaissance, evade static signatures, and orchestrate rapid intrusions across critical infrastructure, software supply chains, and insider pathways.


This has created a critical velocity gap: when adversaries compress attack timelines from days to minutes and defenders rely on manual triage across fragmented legacy tools, the defense falls behind. To secure our most critical infrastructure, defense missions, and sovereign data, public sector organizations need unified, automated security operations purpose-built for the environments they protect.


## Advancing sovereign mission assurance and compliance in air-gapped environments


For sovereign and highly regulated customers, operating in completely disconnected, air-gapped environments is a foundational mandate for mission assurance, strict data residency, and regulatory compliance.


While an air-gapped architecture enforces strict isolation against external network exposure, maintaining sovereign mission assurance also requires on-premises security analytics, live telemetry correlation, and continuous threat intelligence to detect


[sophisticated supply chain compromises, advanced attackers, or insider threats](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/identity-security/google-distributed-clouds-air-gapped-approach-to-zero-trust) . Historically, security teams in disconnected environments have had to maintain numerous standalone tools for log management, endpoint detection, host forensics, and incident tracking—creating visibility blind spots and heavy operational toil. Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped addresses this by providing local compute parity on-premises, enabling organizations to maintain advanced telemetry correlation, strict data residency, and continuous compliance without external network exposure.


## Redefining security with Elastic and Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped


[Elastic Security](https://www.elastic.co/blog/google-distributed-cloud-air-gapped-environments) is deeply integrated into Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) air-gapped infrastructure to deliver this sovereign mission assurance. With the launch of our next-generation Security Information and Event Management (SIEMv2) and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDRv2) architecture on Google Distributed Cloud's Operator Infrastructure Release (OIRv2), Google Cloud and Elastic have embedded unified security operations directly into the platform—transitioning security from periodic, human-driven assessments to continuous, workload defense delivered entirely within the air-gapped environment.


By unifying fragmented legacy tools into a single architecture, we reduce the operational burden of managing disparate systems, lower host resource overhead across infrastructure nodes, and uphold a unified


[Zero Trust Strategy for Google Distributed Cloud](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wnX_9_3WMq0) . We solve this natively ensuring sovereign customers don’t have to stitch together custom log forwarders or brittle connectors.


The collaboration integrates proven security capabilities powered by Elastic Security and Google Cloud, providing unified protection, detection, investigation, and response across Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped environments, inclusive of:


-


[Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)](https://www.elastic.co/security/siem) – Ingests, normalizes, and correlates high-volume infrastructure, network, and audit telemetry into a common schema to effectively detect threats across systems and data in an air-gapped environment. Defenders can leverage pre-built detection rules mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, behavioral analytics, and rapid investigative views from a single console.


-


[Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR)](https://www.elastic.co/security/xdr) – Provides active, kernel-level visibility and behavioral protection through a single unified agent to detect and stop advanced memory exploits, polymorphic malware, and lateral movement before execution. This is a key differentiator in reducing high resource overhead with numerous legacy agents in disconnected environments.


-


[Threat Intelligence](https://cloud.google.com/security/products/threat-intelligence?hl=en) – Equips completely disconnected environments with curated frontline insights, indicators of compromise, and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) developed by Mandiant experts to proactively hunt across the threat domain.


-


[SecOps Foundation](https://cloud.google.com/security/mandiant) – Delivers the operational foundation to build and scale security operations programs, including built-in case management, incident response plans, documentation, runbooks, and standard operating procedures paired with Mandiant service offerings to accelerate deployment.


## The path forward


Disconnected networks relying on manual, human-paced triage across legacy tools cannot keep pace with modern cyber threats. By launching integrated SIEMv2 and EDRv2 capabilities on Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped, Google Cloud and Elastic are empowering sovereign nations, defense agencies, and regulated organizations to shift from fragmented, reactive monitoring to unified, automated defense today.


See a demo of this collaboration in action at the


[Google Public Sector Summit](https://events.govexec.com/google-public-sector-summit/) in Washington, D.C., on October 20, 2026. Google and Elastic will be on-site to show how Elastic Security supports Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped environments—bringing unified prevention, kernel-level detection, behavioral analytics, and native workflow automation to sovereign customers.
